text: Why must long-range electrostatic interactions in MD simulations typically be handled with Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) rather than a simple distance cutoff?
choices: Coulomb interactions decay only as 1/r, too slowly to truncate accurately, so PME splits the calculation into real-space and reciprocal-space sums for roughly O(N log N) efficiency
PME is required only for coarse-grained simulations using MARTINI beads
Simple distance cutoffs are more accurate than PME for every kind of system
Electrostatic interactions decay exponentially, so a cutoff of about 2 angstroms is always sufficient
explanation: Coulomb interactions decay slowly, as 1/r, so naive truncation introduces significant artifacts; PME implements the Ewald sum efficiently by splitting it into short-range real-space and long-range reciprocal-space components, reducing cost from about O(N^1.5) to O(N log N). PME is standard for atomistic (not just coarse-grained) simulations, simple cutoffs are generally less accurate for charged or polar systems, and electrostatics do not decay exponentially.
